implementation.test: Standalone Python parent spawns bounded Python idle and busy subprocesses; uses resource.getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF) and RUSAGE_CHILDREN before/after subprocess.run completion

negative_control_note: Initial 5x busy/idle ratio failed due expensive Python startup (~1 s) even for idle children. Preserved as measurement pitfall; corrected fixed quantitative comparison confirms >0.20 s incremental workload CPU, no attempt to hide startup from total CPU.
limitations: resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN only accounts completed/reaped children; not active concurrent child attribution
RUSAGE_CHILDREN can include unrelated children reaped during interval
Windows needs independent process CPU/cgroup/job object proof
No Go binary IPC/Go process accounting in this gate
No peak resident memory, power, concurrency, or wall-to-CPU efficiency validation
No actual proficiency or authenticated world interaction measured

next_gate.goal: Native Go IPC CPU + Windows resource accounting qualification using genuine source-only binaries; no new Farama source episodes
requirements: isolated Go child workloads with parent-vs-child CPU attribution
Windows independently qualified process time including descendants
separate startup overhead from per-update learning but include both in full total cost
do not promote without actual original-world proficiency
